# Egami.Fonts.Substitutes: guide for coding agents

Egami.Fonts.Substitutes bundles open fonts that stand in for the fonts documents name most, for Egami.Fonts: Liberation Sans,
Serif and Mono for Helvetica, Arial, Times, Times New Roman, Courier and Courier New, Carlito for Calibri and Caladea for Cambria,
each in regular, bold, italic and bold italic. Every glyph has the width of the font it replaces, so text keeps its line breaks.
Use it where documents, metafiles or System.Drawing code name fonts the machine does not have, such as on Linux servers.

Namespaces: `Egami.Fonts.Substitutes`, with `Egami.Fonts`.

## Egami's vocabulary

Egami has its own names. Use them, not names from other imaging libraries: Egami has no `Image` type, no `Mutate` or `Clone`
and no `Configuration`.

- `Raster` and `Raster<TPixel>` hold an image; `TPixel` is a pixel type such as `Rgba8`, `Rgb8`, `Gray8`, `Bgra8` or `RgbaF32`
  (namespace `Egami.Pixels`). `Raster.Load` returns the type that fits the file; `Raster.Load<Rgba8>` converts while decoding.
- `Raster.Probe` reads a file's size, format and orientation without decoding it.
- `Apply(ops => ...)` changes a raster in place through a chain of operations; `Derive(ops => ...)` returns a new raster.
  `As<TPixel>()` converts to a new raster and `Copy()` duplicates one.
- `Save(path)` picks the writer from the extension; `Save(stream, format, options)` names it. Loading always detects the format
  from the bytes, never from the extension.
- `EgamiContext` holds the settings, `SafetyLimits`, thread count and registered formats a call uses. It is immutable: change
  it with `with`, and pass it to `Load` or `Probe`, or make it the default once at startup with `EgamiContext.SetDefault`.
- Every `Raster` owns pooled pixel memory: dispose it, best with `using`. `Derive`, `As` and `Load` return new rasters that you
  dispose too.

## Entry points

- `SubstituteFonts.Find(family, style)`: the stand-in for a family name, or null when there is none.
- `SubstituteFonts.Collection`: all twenty faces as a `FontCollection`.
- Egami.Metafiles takes them through `MetafileRenderOptions.Fonts`; Egami.SystemDrawing through
  `SystemDrawingOptions.FontSubstitutes = SubstituteFonts.Find`.

## Samples

```csharp
// Bundled faces for the fonts documents name most, on any machine: Arial is Liberation Sans, Calibri is Carlito.
Typeface? arial = SubstituteFonts.Find("Arial", FontStyle.Bold);
Font body = new(SubstituteFonts.Find("Calibri", FontStyle.Normal)!, 11);

// All twenty faces as a collection, matched by family name and style.
FontMatch? mono = SubstituteFonts.Collection.Match("Liberation Mono", FontStyle.Italic);
```

Metafiles drawn with the substitutes first, then the installed fonts:

```csharp
// The same pictures on a machine without Arial or Calibri: the bundled substitutes first, then the installed fonts.
var fonts = new FontCollection();
foreach (FontFamily family in SubstituteFonts.Collection)
{
    foreach (Typeface face in family.Faces)
    {
        fonts.Add(face);
    }
}

fonts.AddSystemFonts();
using Raster<Rgba8> image = Metafile.Load(path).Rasterize<Rgba8>(new MetafileRenderOptions { Fonts = fonts });
```

## Common mistakes

- Using `Find` for any family. It knows only the families above; check for null and fall back to installed or shipped fonts.
- Expecting the same glyph shapes as the original. Widths match, the design does not.
